exercise1.prompt: Comment on the difference between a class and an object, then print the blueprint explanation

cases.name: prints an explanation built on the blueprint idea
cases.describe: a printed message that uses the blueprint idea

hiddenCases.name: the explanation covers the object side as well
hiddenCases.describe: the message says what the object is, not only what the class is

hiddenCases.name: a comment says what a class is
hiddenCases.describe: a comment about what a class is

exercise1.hint: Two separate things are being asked for. A comment is for the reader of the code and starts with #; the printed message is for whoever runs it. Both have to be there.

exercise2.prompt: Dog attributes as variables and a bark function, printed and called

cases.name: prints the dog information and the bark

hiddenCases.name: bark is a function, and it is actually called
hiddenCases.describe: a bark function that is defined and then called

exercise2.hint: Behaviour goes in a function; data goes in variables. Defining bark is only half of it -- something has to call it for the bark to happen.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
choices: A class is one object out of many
A class is the blueprint, an object is one thing built from it
They are two words for the same thing
questions.explain: One class can produce any number of objects. Each object carries its own data but shares the structure the class described.

questions.prompt: Which of these are reasons to reach for a class rather than loose variables and functions?
choices: The data and the behaviour that acts on it belong together
You need many things of the same shape, each with its own values
The program has more than ten lines
You want the code to run faster
questions.explain: Classes are about grouping related data with the behaviour that uses it, and about making many of the same shape. Length and speed are not the reason.

questions.prompt: Match each OOP word to what it means.
right: A function that belongs to a class
A blueprint describing what things of this kind have and do
A piece of data belonging to an object
One thing built from a blueprint
questions.explain: Attributes are what an object has, methods are what it does, and the class is the description both come from.

questions.prompt: A house built from a plan is to the plan as an ___ is to a ___.
questions.explain: The plan exists once; the houses built from it are many, and each one has its own address and paint colour.
